page: Microsoft Azure HX176-144rs is an x86_64 architecture server instance within the HX family, running on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. It features 144 dedicated vCPUs powered by an Intel processor. The hardware configuration includes 1408.0 GB of system memory, yielding a resource density of 9.78 GB of RAM per core. For local storage, the instance is equipped with 4332 GB of NVMe SSD capacity. It does not include any graphics processing units.

This server type is RDMA capable and supports Premium Storage. The combination of high-density dedicated compute cores, substantial memory capacity, and fast local NVMe SSD storage provides a balanced profile for resource-intensive workloads. From a qualitative cost-efficiency perspective, the dedicated CPU allocation and high memory-to-core ratio position this instance as a high-density resource pool, minimizing the need for multi-node overhead in memory-bound scenarios.

Given its hardware specifications, the HX176-144rs is suited for large-scale databases, memory-intensive enterprise applications, high-performance computing simulations requiring RDMA, and complex data processing pipelines. The lack of GPU acceleration makes it less suitable for deep learning training, but its massive memory footprint and fast local storage support heavy transactional and analytical database workloads.
